stories.title: The Top 100 Cubs of all time, No. 90: Jake Weimer
stories.summary: This left-hander had a brief, but solid, career with the Cubs over 120 years ago. Already 29 and with five years worth of minor league experience — back in the day when there were no minor league "systems" as there are today — Weimer was acquired by the Cubs prior to the 1903 season. Obviously no one knew what WAR was back then, but his 1903 season was the equivalent of 5.5 bWAR, with 20 wins and a 2.30 ERA. He issued a lot of walks — 104 — but his 128 strikeouts, in an era when most batters didn't K much, ranked fifth in the National League. The following year, he struck out 177 in 307 innings, the K figure good for third in the league.
